plan.request_plan: Stage 1: Fetch the Zoho Recruit careers list directly with plain HTTP GET requests to https://f22labs.zohorecruit.in/jobs/Careers. Use query param page=<page_number> starting at page=1. No browser rendering is required because verified raw HTML contains the hidden_input:jobs hydration JSON and direct job-detail links. If the list page returns HTML, parse the embedded jobs JSON from the hidden input and also collect each job-detail anchor href from the page. Stage 2: For each discovered job-detail URL sample pattern like https://f22labs.zohorecruit.in/jobs/Careers/<job_id>/<slug>?source=CareerSite, fetch the detail page with plain HTTP GET. Use standard browser-like headers only if needed for basic compatibility (Accept: text/html, User-Agent: a normal desktop browser UA). Do not use regex for extraction; use JSON parsing for embedded blobs and CSS selectors for HTML detail pages.
plan.pagination_plan: Use page-number pagination on the list endpoint. Start with page=1 and increment by 1. Continue requesting page=2, page=3, etc. Stop when the page yields no job records in the embedded jobs JSON and no job-detail links, or when the embedded jobs array is structurally absent/null. Do not infer completion from repeated titles or from a fixed page count; the exact stop condition is an empty/missing jobs list on the fetched page.

plan.india_filter_strategy: Prefer server-side India scoping if the Zoho board exposes a country/location filter parameter in the careers URL or embedded query state; however, the verified evidence only confirms page-number pagination, not a dedicated country filter param. Therefore use client-side structural filtering after fetching list pages. For each job, determine India-ness only from structural location fields, not description text. If a country or country_code field exists in the job JSON or detail HTML, keep jobs where country == 'India' or country_code == 'IN'. If the only structural location value is a bare city name in City/location_raw, resolve country using a small static city->country lookup table authored in code covering major India cities: Bengaluru/Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi/New Delhi, Gurugram/Gurgaon, Noida, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad. If the city matches one of those, treat it as India; if not recognized, set country to null and exclude it from India-only output rather than guessing. Never use substring matching on descriptions, and never rely on checking for the literal text 'India' inside a bare city string.
